text:
Sam (Product): Quick design review for the credentials area — create/rotate/revoke flows. Not blocking but want copy + a11y nits sorted before next week. See mock: https://figma.redwood/keys-mock :eyes:

Zara (Design): Saw it. Main issues: primary CTA in the create modal is confusing (two strong CTAs). Also screen-reader focus order is off when the secret is revealed.

Leo (UX Writer): Agree on CTA hierarchy. Proposal: primary = 'Create key', secondary = 'Show secret' (muted). After create show a single ephemeral panel with clear header and action buttons: 'Copy secret' and 'Done'. Banner: "We will only show this secret once."

Matt (Eng): FYI backend constraint: secret token only returned on create. We cannot re-render it later. UI MUST surface that clearly. Suggested banner text: "This secret is shown once. Save it now — we can't show it again."

Anya (Accessibility): A few a11y points: 1) when the modal closes and the ephemeral panel opens, focus should land on the secret field/button. 2) announce the one-time warning via an aria-live polite region. 3) contrast check: the warning icon color falls below AA on light theme.

Zara (Design): Also about empty state for the keys list — current copy is generic. Suggest centered illustration, CTA 'Create your first key', and a single-line helper: 'Keys let services call Redwood APIs. Assign scopes for least privilege.' Keep it simple and don't push a modal on first-run unless user explicitly clicks.

Sam (Product): Rotation permissions question: if a user doesn't have rotate rights, we want the rotate button visible but disabled with a tooltip that explains why. Needs to be keyboard accessible and screen-reader friendly.

Leo (UX Writer): Tooltip copy suggestion: "You need the 'Key Admin' role to rotate keys. Request access from your org admin." Keep it under 80 chars. For disabled state aria-label: "Rotate (requires Key Admin role)".

Matt (Eng): Revoke flow — we debated 'type to confirm' vs checkbox + reason. Engineering prefers checkbox + optional reason field so we record audit info without forcing heavy typing in quick ops.

Anya (Accessibility): Strongly recommend against requiring typing for destructive actions — it creates friction for keyboard/screen-reader users. Checkbox + text input is fine; ensure labels are programmatic and error feedback is announced.

design-bot: Design review checklist updated: https://figma.redwood/keys-checklist (updated components, focus order notes, color token fixes). :white_check_mark:

Sam (Product): Great thread — I'll consolidate the copy changes and create a PR with the final strings today. @Zara please drop final Figma screens, @Leo please add alternate microcopy variants (short/long), @Anya please sanity-check the a11y items once PR is up. Thanks! :thumbsup:
